chunks: And he (peace be upon him) said:

The sign of faith is that you should prefer truth when it harms you over falsehood when it benefits you; that your speech should not exceed your knowledge; and that you should fear Allah when speaking about others.
ai.seo_question: What are the three signs of true faith according to Imam Ali in Nahj al-Balagha?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (peace be upon him) defines the characteristics of true faith (iman) through three key ethical principles: prioritizing truth despite personal cost, ensuring one's speech does not outpace one's knowledge, and maintaining God-consciousness when speaking about others. In Shia scholarship, this hadith is often cited to illustrate the concept of 'Sidq' (truthfulness) as an internal state of being rather than mere verbal assertion, linking it closely to the purification of the self (Tazkiyah). The emphasis on guarding one's tongue regarding others reflects the broader Islamic ethic of preserving social dignity and avoiding Ghibah (backbiting).

en.sayed-ali-raza: 458. Amīr al-mu’minīn, peace be upon him, said:

Belief means that you should prefer truth (even) when it harms you rather than falsehood (even) when it benefits you; that your words should not be more than your action and that you should fear Allāh when speaking about others.
